requirements: Access to Kalphite Queen's boss encounter and any prerequisite quests, keys, instances, or killcount listed by the linked strategy source.
Use the boss-task Slayer helm or Slayer helmet bonuses when the assignment permits it.
Bring supplies and teleports appropriate to a separate boss trip rather than a normal multi-kill Slayer location.
mechanics: Two phases - ground form best meleed (Keris is the kalphite weapon, use crush), airborne wasp form best ranged. Slayer helm (i) on task is the biggest DPS boost.
Treat this as a boss-specific method: positioning, prayer swaps, phase handling, and death-risk setup should come from the linked source strategy.
Use listed secondary weapons only where their combat style or phase role is relevant.

methods.label: General strategy
methods.summary: Two phases - ground form best meleed (Keris is the kalphite weapon, use crush), airborne wasp form best ranged. Slayer helm (i) on task is the biggest DPS boost.
recommendedFor: Players selecting this boss from the Boss meta-task
steps: Two phases - ground form best meleed (Keris is the kalphite weapon, use crush), airborne wasp form best ranged. Slayer helm (i) on task is the biggest DPS boost.
Bring melee for the crawling form and ranged, magic, or Shadow for the airborne form.

methods.label: Travel and lair access
methods.summary: Reach the Kalphite Lair with ropes unless diary rewards remove that requirement, then use the shortcut after Elite Desert Diary when available.
recommendedFor: players deciding pre- or post-Elite Desert Diary routing
requiredOrKeyItems: Two ropes before hard Desert Diary
86 Agility for the Elite Desert Diary shortcut
steps: Travel west of Shantay Pass to the surface entrance or use diary-supported routes.
Bring two ropes if the hard Desert Diary has not permanently placed them.
Pass through the Kalphite Lair, avoiding or tanking poisonous Kalphite soldiers and guardians.
After Elite Desert Diary, use the 86 Agility shortcut to speed up return trips.
risks: Forgetting ropes can block access before diary completion.
Kalphite soldiers and guardians can poison on the route.
notes: Pre-Elite Desert Diary trips are slower, so flinching and longer trips are more attractive.
Post-Elite Desert Diary routing favours higher-damage, shorter return trips.

methods.label: Two-phase main kill
methods.summary: Melee the crawling form with Keris or crush weapons, then switch to ranged, magic, or Shadow for the airborne form while praying Protect from Magic.
steps: Use melee crush or Keris partisan of breaching on the crawling form.
Use Dragon warhammer or Elder maul special attacks if using melee and ranged to lower Defence.
Walk under the Queen at the start of the airborne phase to avoid giving her an extra attack.
Use Toxic blowpipe, Twisted bow, Bow of faerdhinen, Tumeken's shadow, or Eye of ayak on phase two.
Keep hitpoints above 31 because her ranged and magic attacks always roll a successful hit, even if they can hit zero.
risks: Magic and ranged attacks are very accurate and can stack with worker pressure.
The Queen can hatch Kalphite Workers from nearby cocoons when hit.
notes: Protect from Magic is preferred during both phases, especially in groups where ranged attacks can bounce.
Thralls significantly improve kill speed; Vengeance is an alternative or supplement with Spellbook Swap.

methods.label: Guardian flinch setup
methods.summary: Use the Kalphite Guardians and entrance rope positioning to trap the Queen for low-resource flinching.
recommendedFor: pre-Elite Desert Diary KQ head attempts
prayers: Protect from Melee while positioning guardians
Protect from Missiles while moving the Queen
steps: Enter the lair with Protect from Melee and lure the two Kalphite Guardians near the entrance.
Run back to the entrance rope and stand two tiles south so the guardians line up behind each other.
Turn on Protect from Missiles, run three tiles south of the Queen's south-western tile, then immediately run under her.
With the Queen trapped, step out only to attack and step back under or behind the trap before she can retaliate.
Resummon thralls where possible; they add damage while the Queen is trapped.
risks: The safespot must be rebuilt after each kill.
Existing Kalphite Workers can interfere with resetting the trap unless killed or the world is hopped.
notes: Flinching is slower but uses far fewer supplies and can extend trips to five or more kills.
Verac's equipment can hit through the Queen's high Defence on both forms.
